title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) comparing a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline to accepting an LLM suggestion directly for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Under the preregistered sampling and execution contract we selected K=200 deterministic tasks and used a single shared generator output per task. Observed primary outcome: baseline = 200/200 validator‑compliant applies; guarded = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The repair step was never invoked (repair_applied=false for all guarded episodes). All run artifacts and verifier traces are archived (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4233332164d0453e2aecdb34d52a01883358d67ac30e028e6; preregistration SHA‑256 = a6d73a5cc0bda22e691a3634068a881b36ae274a65ab33919a647ec32c56e622). We interpret this as an artifact‑grounded ceiling/null observation for the tested model/validator/task regime and discuss implications and design lessons for future failure‑rich evaluations.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation is operationally attractive but risky: erroneous changes can cause reachability regressions, outages, or security policy violations. Architectural prescriptions frequently combine generative LLM components with deterministic verifiers and automated repair (generate→verify→repair, G→V→R). Prior work demonstrates pipelines and tooling prototypes, but causal estimates of verifier utility under reproducible, preregistered designs are sparse. We therefore preregistered (study_id = cand-002-gvr-loop) a paired confirmatory experiment that isolates the verifier+repair marginal effect on fixed generator outputs. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, the within‑task difference in binary validator pass rates between accepting a generated candidate directly (baseline) and first passing it through verify→repair (guarded).
sections.related_work: Relevant directions include generate–validate–repair benchmarks and formal verification for NetOps (e.g., Cornetto; generate‑translate‑verify position pieces), work arguing to confine LLMs to translation and rely on solvers/verification, and tool‑assisted agentic NetOps architectures. Our work differs by providing a fully preregistered, artifact‑archived paired causal estimate of verifier marginality under a deterministic sampling and execution contract. We cite and archived-close related artifacts as context (see cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. The study was preregistered before final outcomes (preregistration SHA‑256 = a6d73a5c...). Key design choices (archived): deterministic task selection (SHA‑256(intent_string) sort, first K=200 tasks; manifest: execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a single shared_initial_generation per task that both arms evaluated (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Requested model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). We archived every provider call, candidate, validator trace, and scoring JSON (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...).
sections.results: Execution summary (artifact‑grounded). Planned episodes: 400 (2 arms × 200 tasks). Completed episodes: 400. Model calls used: 200 (shared initial generation only). Complete paired count = 200. Baseline validator passes = 200/200; guarded validator passes = 200/200. Paired contingency: n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...). Primary estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = 52a0858d...). The guarded repair path was never used: repair_applied=false in every guarded scoring JSON (execution/scoring/*.json; representative example execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 = 3055f874...). Representative per‑task validator diagnostics (parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, final_state snapshot) are present in the archived scoring JSONs and in the representative_tasks manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...).
sections.discussion: Statistical interpretation of a degenerate outcome. When no discordant pairs are observed (n10=n01=0), exact paired inference yields p=1.00 and bootstrap percentile intervals collapse to a point mass at zero; this is the mathematically correct descriptive inference for the realized paired sample. The preregistered power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline failure rate (~0.20) and therefore is not applicable post hoc when baseline=0. We executed the planned bootstrap (10k, seed=1729) and report the degenerate CI artifact‑grounded rather than re‑specifying thresholds after seeing data (analysis artifacts archived).
sections.conclusion: Under the preregistered contract (deterministic task sampling that required validator coverage, shared_initial_generation per task, requested_model=gpt-5-mini), all generated candidates satisfied the deterministic validator: baseline = 200/200 and guarded = 200/200. Repair was never triggered. Consequently, the confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R yields a lower regression‑causing change rate than LLM‑only) was not supported in this regime: paired difference = 0.00, McNemar p = 1.00, bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]. This ceiling/null outcome is reproducible from the archived artifacts (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...). It does not imply verifiers are unnecessary in general—rather, it highlights that (i) task sampling, (ii) generator strength, and (iii) estimand choice (shared_initial vs interactive) determine whether repairs can be exercised. We therefore recommend future confirmatory evaluations intentionally sample failure‑rich distributions, vary generator strengths, and consider interactive closed‑loop estimands when the research question concerns end‑to‑end generator–verifier utility. All execution and scoring artifacts are released for replay and audit (execution/ and analysis/; keys and hashes listed in the manuscript evidence bundle).

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt-5-mini): outcomes do not generalize to other LLMs without further experiments.

Deterministic task pool and inclusion rule required validator coverage for selection; this sampling choice biases the sample toward intents the validator already supports and reduces external validity to failure‑rich operational distributions.
Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would mask real regressions (the binary outcome conflates true safety with validator reach).

Design constraint: shared_initial_generation fixes the generator output for both arms and prevents generator adaptation; the experiment therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates, not closed‑loop generator–verifier improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) rendered the preregistered power calculation inapplicable; inference is descriptive and specific to the tested regime.
